correctness.rationale: For \(R=\prod_i\mathbb F_{q_i}\), zero-set classes are maximal false-twin classes and their quotient is the disjointness graph on nonempty proper subsets. Subset size follows from quotient degree, singletons are therefore invariant, and adjacency to them recovers every subset, so the quotient action is the coordinate \(S_r\)-action. In the non-Boolean case every nontrivial fiber must lose at most one vertex, and those forced selected fibers fix all coordinates; conversely the same condition kills every internal transposition and quotient permutation. The polynomial and minimum-set count are then exact independent-fiber products. In the Boolean case all fibers are singletons and a pointwise stabilizer is trivial exactly when coordinate incidence columns are distinct, yielding \(\lceil\log_2r\rceil\). The standalone checker exhaustively verifies four small graph instances and closed-form identities on additional tuples.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete all-set invariant for a standard algebra graph family rather than a single small-case computation. It identifies a sharp structural transition: if any \(q_i>2\), twin multiplicity forces \(|V|-(2^r-2)\) landmarks and a fully factorized determining polynomial; if every \(q_i=2\), the graph becomes a pure coordinate object with determining number only \(\lceil\log_2r\rceil\). The exact classification and minimum-set count make the mechanism reusable for extensions to nonreduced semilocal factors.
